learning_outcomes.text: Students should know how to apply acquired knowledge and problem-solving skills in new or unfamiliar environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study
Students should be able to communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and rationale behind them to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously
Students should possess the learning skills that will allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous way.
Possess adequate knowledge of the scientific and technological aspects of manufacturing.
Design, calculate and engineer products, processes, installations and plants.
Perform research, development, and innovation in products, processes, and methods.
Knowledge and ability to design, calculate and engineer integrated manufacturing systems.
Understanding of the fundamental aspects present in manufacturing systems based on integrated manufacturing strategies.
Knowledge and ability to design, calculate and engineer integrated manufacturing systems.

syllabus_topics: Evolution of manufacturing machines and systems
Definition and classification of industrial robots
Grippers and tools used in industrial robots
Basic configuration of a process control system
Petri nets applied to modeling and analysis of manufacturing systems
assessment_rules: To pass the subject, the overall score must be equal to or greater than 50% of the maximum possible score. The evaluation system applies to all ordinary and extraordinary calls. For differentiated evaluation, a single written exam with two parts will be administered: 75% for theoretical-practical content and 25% for laboratory practices. For group practices, a detailed report must be submitted and defended.
